newsitem.title: FRANCE: Frenchman on trial over Spanish death squads.
newsitem.headline: Frenchman on trial over Spanish death squads.

text.p: A suspected leader of Spain's "dirty war" against Basque separatist rebels appears in an anti-terrorist court in the French Pyrenean town of Pau on Monday at the start of the first such trial held in France.

Frenchman Georges Mendaille, who was extradited from Spain two years ago, is suspected of having ordered the death squad killing of several Basque refugees in France and he faces charges of being an accomplice to murder.
Death squad henchmen convicted in France have accused Mendaille of giving them instructions, but they later withdrew their allegations.
Mendaille has denied the charges and said he had infiltrated Spain's Anti-Terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL) death squads on behalf of France's DST counter-espionnage services.
GAL squads killed 28 people between 1983 and 1987, mostly in southern France. The group said it acted in retaliation for killings in Spain by ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) separatist guerrillas.

Several Spanish high officials and former security chiefs have been charged at home with running the death squads. The scandal contributed to last year's election defeat of former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez's Socialists to the conservatives of the current prime minister, Jose Aznar.
